T85: the companion's persona choice must actually be DELIVERED, and the gate that proves it was never being run (registered 2026-08-31). tools/companion_delivery_gate.py has existed and PASSES standalone - persona_resolution current=0 baseline=0 - but it appeared ZERO times in this file, so the board never executed it. T85 sat at `locking` 90% naming `companion-delivery` in its artifacts, and validate_trajectory_registry let that stand because rule 5 requires a `locking` row to NAME a gate without checking the name RESOLVES. So the registry asserted a lock, the script existed, the script passed - and nothing connected the three. ★THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS FOUND TWICE MORE TODAY, which is why it is worth a long label: 96 psql recipes carried a `replay` line and nothing ever re-ran them (fixed by the psql-probe-suite gate), and 16 of 20 locked trajectories rest on gates reading SKIP because full boards were dying on KeyError: 'args'. A lock nothing runs locks nothing, and the three failure modes are indistinguishable from the outside - unregistered, unrun, and skipped all look exactly like green. The gate itself is the pre-existing companion delivery check (persona resolution against its baseline); registering it is the whole fix, and it makes T85's claim true rather than aspirational.

T-arc boundary_not_emptiness, held as a forward-only line (2026-08-31). 34 bank rows carry ONE oracle - 'a permission boundary reads as not-visible-with-this-session, never as nothing-here' - and no gate covered it: empty-state-discrimination is about search-0 vs first-run, failed-read-is-not-empty is about a read that ERRORED, auth-boundary is about whether the server refuses. This is the third thing: the read SUCCEEDED, the server lawfully returned nothing, and the question is whether the page says 'you cannot see this' or 'there is nothing here'. ★WHY IT IS HARD AND WHY MOST SURFACES FAIL IT: RLS refuses by FILTERING, not raising - a USING clause returns zero rows and no error, so a foreign-hive read and a genuinely empty hive are byte-identical at the client unless the page makes a separate membership check and has somewhere to say so. MEASURED across 42 root surfaces: 26 own an absence state and 10 of those carry NO refusal copy at all. ★THAT NUMBER READ 25 FIRST AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, TWICE OVER, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE COUNT: the vocabulary was narrower than the product's ('needs a hive'; 'Create or join a Hive' where the regex knew only 'join or create'; 'does not have access' where it knew only 'do not'), AND an edit wrote literal BACKSPACE bytes (0x08) where   word-boundaries were intended, so the join/create clause demanded a backspace character in page text and could never fire. It went 25 -> 24 -> 22 -> 10 with no page changing. A census whose vocabulary is narrower than the product's measures its own wording and invents backlog - here, 2.5x the real one. The scenario is ordinary - a worker removed from a hive keeps wh_active_hive_id in localStorage, their next read is lawfully filtered to zero, and pm-scheduler answers 'No completions recorded yet.' ★THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE FIX PATTERN, ALREADY IN THIS REPO: marketplace.html:1222-1226 keeps _rateLimited (429 + the wait), _authExpired (401, 'the remedy is signing in, not retrying') and _accessDenied ('a 403 is a REFUSED ROW with a perfectly good session, and signing in again cannot fix it'), reset per load so a since-granted permission stops reading as denied. So the work for the other 25 is to propagate an idiom this codebase already reasoned about. ★AND EVEN THAT EXCEPTION ONLY COVERS THE LOUD HALF: _accessDenied fires on a 403 the server announces; the silent case - RLS filtering, 200 with zero rows - is invisible to any HTTP status and needs the membership read. ★A RATCHET, NOT A FAIL, ON PURPOSE: 25 of 26 fail today, and a gate that is red the day it ships is one people learn to scroll past; this repo's ordering is fix first then enforce (retry_path did the same). The count may FALL, never rise - a NEW surface shipping an empty state with no way to say a refusal happened fails here by name. Comments are stripped before counting, because the first pass credited inventory.html with four refusal states that were every one a source comment or the toast 'Part removed from inventory.' Teeth proven by dropping a surface from the baseline: the check names it and fails.

T70: a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. The seller profile is where a buyer decides whether to trust a stranger with money, so every pixel that reads as an endorsement is a claim the PLATFORM makes on that stranger's behalf - and the recorded incident shows what an unenforced one costs: the 'Certified' chip used to render on the cert_verified flag ALONE across three surfaces, and three sellers were found with cert_verified true, certifications NULL and cert_verified_at NULL, a violet chip asserting an admin had verified trade credentials THAT DID NOT EXIST. CENSUSED EVERY TRUST CLAIM ON THE PROFILE and the page is in good order - each is computed from data rather than decoration: Top rated (ratingAvg >= 4.5 AND ratingCount >= 5), Quick reply (avgResponseHours < 4 AND replyCount >= 5), Tier (stated thresholds - silver 11 sales, gold 51 - plus 'set by WorkHive from completed sales, not self-assigned'), ID Verified (gated on kyb_verified), Certified (routed through whCertBadgeEarned on all three surfaces). ★ONE LOOKED LIKE THE ORIGINAL BUG AND IS NOT: the certifications SECTION reads cert_verified on its own, but the whole block sits inside `if (certSection && certs.length)`, so a non-empty list is guaranteed by construction - read before accusing. THE ASSERTION guards the fixed class rather than a present defect: no buyer-facing surface may present a certification claim from cert_verified alone; it must call the central predicate or guard on the certifications list in the same breath. ★MODERATION SURFACES ARE EXCLUDED BY NAME, and not for convenience: marketplace-admin, founder-console and platform-actions are where verification is GRANTED, so they must see the raw flag including the exact 'set but no certifications on file' state this gate keeps off a buyer's screen - blinding the moderator to what they moderate would invert the goal. Teeth proven by reverting the profile badge to the flag alone, which resurrects the original incident's shape.

T87/AI6: the RENDER half of machine authorship. validate_ai_write_provenance proves the WRITE half at 6/6 - every AI write into a human-read domain table declares machine authorship ON THE ROW - and that is necessary but not sufficient, because a row can carry its provenance faithfully while the page throws it away on the way to the screen. ★THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT WAS HAPPENING: logbook's 'past repairs on this machine' panel, the one a technician reads BEFORE OPENING A MACHINE, queried fault_knowledge selecting only problem/root_cause/action/knowledge/worker_name/created_at and rendered each row attributed BY NAME. fault_knowledge is a table the AI also writes into (visual-defect-capture), so a machine-captured observation would have appeared as a repair a named colleague performed. The write was accountable; the READ discarded the accountability. Fixed: the select now fetches source and ai_model, and the render appends 'AI-captured (<model>)' beside the name - verified live with a seeded row, one badge among five, the four human entries untouched, probe removed and residue re-counted 0. ★THE BADGE TESTS source LIKE 'ai_%', NOT != 'manual', because that is the contract the DATABASE enforces - CHECK ((source ~~ 'ai\_%') = (ai_model IS NOT NULL)) over a closed vocabulary of manual / ai_visual_capture / cmms_import - so the badge cannot drift from the guarantee, and cmms_import (an import, not a machine author) is correctly left unmarked. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS, ALL CAUGHT BY THE TEETH TEST: blanking comments with plain spaces preserved byte offsets but destroyed LINE numbers, so it first reported the finding at an Escape-key handler; a .select('id') after an .update() was mistaken for a display read when it is an optimistic-concurrency no-op detector; and a 600-char scan window ended before logbook's own .select() because the explanatory comment above it is ~700 chars - the gate silently stopped seeing the query it was built for and reported PASS with the fix reverted. A window sized to today's code narrows every time someone documents something.

T177: the platform must teach its own vocabulary. WorkHive puts domain acronyms straight onto the glass - MTBF beside a number, OEE on a card, SPI in a project summary. For a reliability engineer that is correct and efficient; for the audience this platform explicitly courts - new graduates, workers coming off paper - an unexplained acronym is a number they can neither act on nor argue with, and 'I did not understand the screen' is indistinguishable from 'the screen was wrong'. THE RULE: every registered term appearing in an app page's visible text must be EXPLAINED somewhere reachable - expanded in place, or taught in the learn cluster. Both count, because a guide is a real answer and so is a phrase in the sentence itself. MEASURED 2026-08-26: thirteen terms on the glass and ELEVEN were already handled well - MTBF, MTTR, OEE, RCM, FMEA, RPN, CPM, LOTO, SOP and P-F each have a learn guide spelling them out, which says the platform's teaching habit is sound. ★THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: project-manager showed supervisors 'EVM: SPI 0.87, CPI 1.02, status ... (BAC ₱..., EV ₱...)' - SIX acronyms in a single line - and nothing anywhere on the platform explained one of them; earned value was the only vocabulary the product used without teaching. Fixed at FIRST USE in that line ('Earned value (EVM): schedule performance SPI ..., cost performance CPI ..., ... (budget at completion ₱..., earned value ₱...)'), because a glossary a reader has to go and find is a glossary they do not read. ★assistant.html IS EXCLUDED WITH ITS REASON: it carries a capability CATALOG describing every other page to the model ('...daily progress, EV/SPI/CPI, and sign-off'), which is model-facing rather than UI and double-counts vocabulary belonging to the pages it names - pages this gate scans on their own. Flagging it would demand a glossary inside a system prompt. Teeth proven by reverting the fix, which reproduces the exact pre-fix finding.

T182: a message shown too briefly was never shown. A toast is how this platform says 'saved', 'not saved', 'you cannot do that yet' - the entire receipt for most actions - and a receipt that vanishes before it can be read is WORSE than none, because the action looks silent so the person repeats it. Not hypothetical here: the recorded incident had nine REFUSALS displayed for zero milliseconds, i.e. never displayed at all, on exactly the paths where the user most needed to know why they were stopped. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the class is EXTINCT: 937 showToast calls, 906 on their page's default and 31 with an explicit duration, all between 4000 and 7000ms; every one of the 27 per-page showToast implementations holds its toast 2200-3500ms; nothing anywhere is under 1500ms. TWO ASSERTIONS, guarding an absence rather than fixing a present defect: no call passes an explicit duration below the floor, and no implementation holds its message for less. ★THE FLOOR IS 1500ms AND DELIBERATELY LOW - this gate does not litigate whether 3000 beats 3500, a judgement 27 pages have already made sensibly and which a gate would only turn into enforced taste; it catches what is objectively broken, a message a human cannot finish reading. ★THE CENSUS PARSES ARGUMENTS RATHER THAN SCANNING A WINDOW, and that is the lesson: a first version looked for the nearest ', <number>)' after each call and reported ten short toasts, EVERY ONE FALSE - it had matched slice(0, 24), setTimeout(..., 60) and other numerics belonging to different calls entirely, including a '24ms toast' in utils.js that does not exist. Only balanced-paren splitting knows which arguments belong to which call. Teeth proven on both assertions.

T180: every form control says what it is. A control with no accessible name is a box a screen-reader user is asked to fill in without being told what goes in it - and on this platform that was not theoretical: the unnamed ones were a PM frequency selector, a CMMS column mapper, a scope-item include checkbox and its estimated-hours field, each sitting in a LIST of near-identical rows where 'combo box' announced twelve times running is indistinguishable from noise. Fixed six, and every label names the ROW rather than the field, because these are heard out of visual context: 'Frequency for <task text>', 'Source column for <field label>', 'Include scope item <title>', 'Estimated hours for <title>', plus two validator-catalog filters sitting beside a search box that already had one. Verified in the LIVE DOM on all four pages (0 unnamed, 0 pageerrors), which also covers the dynamically-rendered controls a static pass cannot reach. ★THE CENSUS WAS WRONG THREE TIMES AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE REAL CONTENT: 41 -> 18 -> 8 -> 6, every step removing FALSE accusations rather than real defects. (1) Checking only label[for=id] missed the WRAPPING form - '<label>Safety-critical <input type=checkbox></label>' - which needs no `for` and is how every checkbox and radio here is labelled; that alone was 23 wrong accusations including all six of hive.html's intent radios. (2) Reading raw source matched <input> and <select> written inside HTML, CSS and JS COMMENTS - prose DESCRIBING controls, like logbook's 'A filter <select> may not be squeezed narrower than the option it is showing' - so 62 of the 311 'controls' were sentences. (3) Two survivors were labelled by TEMPLATE INTERPOLATION: resume.html builds `const _alab = aria-label="..."` and injects ${_alab} into the tag, an attribute that is real at runtime and invisible to a static reader. The gate therefore SKIPS any control whose attributes carry an unresolved ${...} and REPORTS the count, because a static oracle must decline what it cannot know rather than guess. ★PLACEHOLDER IS NOT ACCEPTED AS A NAME: it vanishes the moment the field is focused, which is exactly when the reminder is needed.

T179: one glyph, one meaning. An icon-only control teaches by repetition - a worker learns that a small x makes something go away, and after the tenth time they stop reading and just tap. That learned reflex is the whole value of an icon and the whole danger, because the moment the same glyph does something ELSE, the reflex fires anyway. CENSUSED every icon-only button across the app pages; five glyphs in use, two carrying trouble. ✕ meant Close, Remove, AND 'Delete resume <title>' - the same mark for 'dismiss this panel' and for 'permanently destroy the resume you spent an hour building'. Fixed by adopting the platform's OWN declared delete glyph (audit-log.html:790 maps edit '✎', delete '🗑'), so the resume delete is a wastebasket and ✕ is left meaning dismiss. × appeared on three project-manager buttons carrying title='Remove' and NO aria-label: ★THE TITLE DOES NOT SAVE IT, because the accessible-name order is aria-labelledby, aria-label, CONTENT, then title - content wins, a screen reader announces 'multiplication sign' and never reaches the title, and on touch there is no hover at all. Each now names what it removes ('Remove scope item <title>', 'Remove link <label>', 'Remove <name> from this project'), since three identical 'Remove' buttons in one list are their own kind of unusable. Also found and named a bare ← in logbook's multi-step entry form, sitting directly beside Save Entry where the difference between going back and saving is the user's whole entry. TWO ASSERTIONS: every icon-only button has an accessible name beyond its glyph, and no glyph carries both a DISMISS meaning and a DESTROY meaning. ★TWO SCOPING DECISIONS, both stated rather than silent: 'Remove' is NOT treated as destroy - taking a link off a list is undoable list-editing, and lumping it with delete would force a second glyph for something users correctly read as dismissal; and icon-ONLY means nothing but the glyph, after an earlier 'at most 3 other characters' allowance flagged six perfectly good icon+label buttons ('⬇ CSV', '⬇ PDF', '🟢 Low') whose visible text already IS their accessible name. Teeth proven on both assertions, the clash half being a true resurrection against the pre-fix ✕.

C7 (critic deepwalk T9): RECEIPT TOASTS QUEUE instead of stomping. Walked live: a logbook save fires 'Entry saved' + '+15 XP' + a badge back-to-back and the single toast slot REPLACED each with the next in ~0ms (clearTimeout + overwrite) - the worker read only the last receipt; the XP receipt vanished unread on every save. Proven live: the exact three-receipt burst showed sequentially at 0/2.8/5.6s, each full-length. Three static legs with per-leg resurrection teeth. T42 (critic deepwalk): MODALS TRAP BACK. Walked live: opening inventory's Add-Part modal pushed no history entry, so the phone hardware-Back gesture navigated away from the WHOLE page mid-form (inventory -> logbook, task + typed input gone); no page implemented modal-back-to-close. Fixed in the ONE shared primitive every hand-rolled modal already opts into (whModalA11y/whSheetA11y): activate() pushes {whModalBack:true}, a shared popstate handler closes the TOP open modal via its OWN close path (the same logic Escape uses), and deactivate() consumes the entry with a suppressed history.back() when the modal closed any other way (X/backdrop/save) so no ghost states accumulate. Proven live on the walked defect: Back dismissed the modal and STAYED on inventory; after an X-close the stack drained (next Back exits cleanly). 2026-10-12 (UFAI W4791): the give-back history.back() reached every OTHER popstate listener as if the person pressed Back - skillmatrix's Take Exam opened the exam and two listeners closed it at once (the exam could not be taken); teaching only those sent the click to index.html, because Chrome resolves the back() before the exam's push. Now: the give-back is deferred a task and issued as ONE counted whBookkeepingBack(n), a modal opening in the same turn takes the entry over, and EVERY popstate listener in a shipped page asks whIsBookkeepingBack() first (or is marked wh-popstate-reconciler). Gate: 5 utils legs + a scan of every shipped popstate listener; self-test reddens on each leg and on a planted naked or named listener.

Cluster 1 (critic deepwalk): every rendered timestamp keeps ONE clock, and the ops-home shift line is plant-anchored + labeled. Walked live 2026-09-02 at GMT+12: logbook's card read 'Sep 1, 2026 - 12:09 AM' for a save made at 20:09 Manila - whFmtDate pinned the DATE to Asia/Manila while toLocaleTimeString (no timeZone) floated the TIME on the viewer's clock: a pair no clock on earth shows, and any worker east of UTC logging after local midnight filed under yesterday. A ratchet on DEVICE-CLOCK day boundaries (2026-10-13). WorkHive's day is the Manila day, and four critique rows the same day found code taking 'today', 'now', a greeting or 'since midnight' from the device instead (dayplanner 8 sites, hive 3, pm-scheduler, project-report) - on Ian's own New Zealand host, and on the home page itself, whose 'today' window for get_hive_dashboard opened at 19:00 Manila the day before (fixed and walked on an Auckland and a London clock: p_day_start is Manila midnight on both). Counts, in code with comments stripped, on every production page and root shared script: setHours(0,0,0,0), toISOString().slice(0,10), toLocaleDateString with no timeZone, new Date().getHours/getDay/getDate. 150 sites in 20 files on the day it was built (89 were engineering-design.js report date stamps), all cleared the same day - pinned to Manila through the new utils.js whManilaYmd / whManilaMidnight, or marked device-clock-allow where the math was already Manila or pure UTC date arithmetic; the baseline is 0, so ANY new device-clock day boundary fails. 'device-clock-allow: <why>' marks a site that really means the viewer's clock, or local-field math on a date already shifted to Manila. Teeth: the pre-fix pm-scheduler daysLabel reddens; each pattern bites its own shape; Manila-pinned, commented and allow-marked forms do not.

T29: a deep-linked team search survives init and keeps ALL-history scope. The alert->asset->'Fault history' chain hands off to logbook.html?q=<tag>&view=team; walked live 2026-09-02 (Pablo, PV-002) the supervisor-default init re-ran setViewMode('team') AFTER the URL handler had started searchTeam(), wiping the in-flight results back to the browse prompt - 36 real team rows invisible to the exact persona who walks the diagnostic chain (workers skip that branch, so only supervisors broke). Second half: loadTeamMembers() lands a 7-day date default ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so even a surviving hand-off got silently re-scoped to a week on the next search - 'has this failed before' is an all-history question, and the scoped-zero card's own copy admitted it ('Only that date range was searched - it is not proof the entry does not exist'). Static shape-lock with resurrection teeth: the pre-fix unguarded default and an unconditional window both redden the self-test. Fix verified live: the same deep-link now renders 30 cards all-time.
