§BRH.10 AL (2026-10-26): a release never ships ahead of the data move its pages read. The 2026-10-24 release shipped pages that read only a photo's stored path while production's copy pass had not run - 22 logbook and 5 part photos showed nothing until it ran on 2026-10-26. Each data move names the code fact that makes a release depend on it and the production rows still owing it; production is asked through PostgREST with the linked CLI's service key. The pre-push release gate runs it with --require-prod (a production that cannot be asked blocks the push); a run with no way to ask production (CI) says so and passes.

T171: what an ISO-minded evaluator would check. Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language, and the headline result is good AND worth stating precisely, because 'we claim no certifications' is easy to assert and had never been verified: there is NO WorkHive self-certification anywhere - no SOC 2, no ISO 27001, no 'GDPR-compliant', no HIPAA, no PCI-DSS, no bank-grade or military-grade security. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★THE ONE REAL OVERCLAIM WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, NOT A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook said WorkHive logbook entries 'SATISFY Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'SATISFIES Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'SATISFY Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - a tool holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity - and the sentence reads as reassurance, so a plant could walk into a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1', plus a callout stating the distinction outright: same value claimed, no false comfort. Live-verified rendering, 0 pageerrors. TWO ASSERTIONS: (clause) no feature may satisfy/meet/fulfil a NUMBERED clause - and note what is deliberately NOT caught, since 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both appear on that same page and are both fine, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need; only a numbered clause as the object is the error; (selfcert) no page may claim a certification the platform lacks - zero today, guard-the-absence, because that is the single most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both.

T162: a promise to re-check is a promise. The competitor-comparison pages are the most perishable content on the platform and they are written WELL - every competitor price dated ('published entry pricing, August 2026'), sourced ('vendor published pricing and feature pages, accessed August 2026'), caveated ('SaaS pricing moves, confirm current terms with the vendor'), and generous to the competition ('the strongest mobile-first product in the category'). Nothing in the comparisons themselves needed fixing. ★THE RISK IS HIDDEN INSIDE THAT QUALITY: each page also prints 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026' and 'This comparison is reviewed quarterly for pricing and feature accuracy'. Those are not descriptions, they are COMMITMENTS with a clock running - and left alone they decay into the worst kind of claim, an explicit confident promise of currency printed beside prices nobody has re-checked in a year. A reader trusts the page MORE because of that sentence, which is precisely what makes it expensive when it stops being true. THE ASSERTION: where a page states a verification date AND a review cadence, the date must still be inside the cadence it promised (quarterly = 92 days). Measured 2026-08-26: 3 pages, all verified 5 August 2026, 21 days old and comfortably inside. ★THIS GATE IS BUILT TO GO RED - around 5 November 2026 for these three, unless someone re-verifies. That is the point, not a defect: it converts a marketing sentence into a maintained obligation, and the fix when it fires is a real one (re-check the prices and move the date, or delete the commitment). NO GRACE PERIOD, deliberately - the page names its own cadence, so the cadence is the bar; the passing output prints the days remaining so it arrives as a countdown rather than a surprise. Teeth proven by ageing one date to 5 January: 233d against a 92d promise, exit 1.

T161: content ages with supervision, not heroics. A statistic on a public page is a claim a reader - or an answer engine - will repeat, and the dangerous shape is not an OLD year but a year that silently became a LIE: 'as of 2024, the average plant...' was true when written and is quietly false now, because nobody re-reads a sentence that already shipped. ★THE INVENTORY CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE ASSERTS, and that is the lesson: a first pass across 114 public pages flagged 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY; flagging them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely, the exact opposite of the goal, and 33 false findings on the way. SO IT ASSERTS THE SHAPE, NOT THE AGE. Two things rot and neither is a citation: (as-of) a present-tense claim pinned to a past year - 'as of 2024', 'currently ... 2023', 'latest figures 2022' - allowed only within the current year and the two before it, the window SLIDING with the clock so the gate keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it; and (future) a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or a template copy, which reads as authoritative until someone checks. BOTH ARE ZERO TODAY across 115 pages - this is a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, because a property that holds by CARE rather than by structure lapses in silence. Teeth proven on both shapes at once: an injected 'as of 2021' and a '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1.

T154: machine-readable truth = human-readable truth. JSON-LD is what an answer engine QUOTES when it cites this platform, and nobody proofreads it because nobody SEES it - so it drifts away from the page underneath and keeps being served, confidently, to the machines that summarize us. TWO CONTRACTS, both born from real drift. FAQ: every FAQPage Question name must appear in the page's visible text - the class T1 caught on the landing page, where the LD still told the provisioning-waitlist story after the page had moved to instant signup; an FAQ rich result PROMISES the page answers that question, so if the words are not there the promise is to content that does not exist (508 questions across 115 public pages, all present). NAME: an Article headline must still be recognisable as the page's own og:title/<title> - FOUND HERE, predictive-alert-thresholds-plants had been retitled to lead with 'ISO 10816 Vibration Thresholds and Predictive Alert Limits', a deliberate move toward the citable standard, while its LD headline kept the older vaguer 'Predictive Alert Thresholds for Industrial Plants', so an answer engine reading the structured data got the version WITHOUT the ISO anchor that makes the page worth citing (synced; 53 headlines now match). ★HowToStep NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE FINDING: a first pass flagged 31 'gaps' across 12 HowTo pages and every one was editorial paraphrase - the OEE guide's LD says 'Measure planned production time' where the page heads that section 'Step 1: Planned Production Time'. Same step, different register. A step name is a LABEL for a procedure; demanding substring identity would have shipped 31 false findings and taught everyone to ignore this gate. The FAQ question and the headline are different in kind - both are read VERBATIM by their consumers, so identity is the actual contract there. Teeth proven on BOTH halves: a fabricated question and a reverted headline, 2 flagged, exit 1.

T158: a canonical must name a URL that EXISTS. rel=canonical is a claim - 'the real version of this page lives here' - and when the URL it names does not exist, the page tells every crawler its authoritative copy is at nothing. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26, VERIFIED AGAINST PRODUCTION rather than inferred: workhiveph.com/workhive/public-feed.html returned 404 while workhiveph.com/public-feed.html returned 200, and FIFTEEN pages shipped the dead form - a /workhive/ segment left over from an earlier deploy path, still being served long after the site moved to the domain root. ★WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY EXISTING CHECK: they all asked whether a canonical was PRESENT, and all 15 were present, well-formed, absolute and unique - and pointed at a 404. Presence is the easy half of a claim; this gate checks the half that costs something. ★THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST was public-feed, the anonymous shop window and the only one of the 15 meant to be found by strangers: a shared link to it carried a signal saying the real page was elsewhere, at a URL that does not resolve. Now 145 on-site canonicals all name a page that exists. STATIC BY DESIGN - the path IS the defect, and a live HTTP check would make the gate depend on the network to state a fact about a string. TEETH PROVEN by re-breaking public-feed's canonical: 1 flagged, exit 1.

T160: the SEO funnel must not jump while you read it. CLS is where a page loses a searcher without erroring - text settles, the reader's eye is already moving, and the line they were on is somewhere else - and on the funnel it costs twice, because Core Web Vitals feed ranking, so the pages most dependent on search were the ones shifting. MEASURED, ISOLATED, THEN FIXED. The learn template shifted 0.384 CLS at 390, nearly 4x the 0.1 bar. ★THE RECORDED SUSPICION WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO: the note blamed an element injected at ~1s, and a MutationObserver armed alongside the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size. The timeline showed a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms; blocking the font stylesheet took CLS to 0.000 while blocking the Tailwind CDN only reached 0.156. The font swap was the whole cause. THE FIX was one parameter - display=swap to display=optional across 113 public pages: optional gives the font ~100ms then never swaps, so the page cannot jump, and measured on a real load it STILL renders Poppins. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is exactly the reader who previously got the jump instead. Verified 0.000 CLS across learn, tools and the landing page. ★IT ASSERTS THE PARAMETER, NOT A CLS NUMBER: a lab CLS reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy, and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored - the parameter is deterministic and it IS the defect.

T3/T153: the calculator pages state the account requirement. The 60 /tools/ pages are the top of the funnel - a searcher looking for 'OEE calculator' lands on one, and what it promises decides whether the next click is trust or a bounce. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the human-facing story is HONEST: none of the 60 embeds a calculator (they are landing pages that explain a calculation and hand off) and every one says so plainly - 'free with a WorkHive account. Sign-up takes about 30 seconds.' ZERO still carry the 'no sign-up needed' claim T3 recorded, which linked into a gated page and was false twice over. The gate keeps a fixed claim fixed, because that wording lived in a TEMPLATE - it came back everywhere at once when it came back at all. ★A RECORDED FINDING IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENFORCE: every one of the 60 declares JSON-LD @type SoftwareApplication with an Offer of price 0 and a url pointing at the LANDING page, so a search or answer engine reads 'there is a free web application here', follows the url, and finds a page about an application that lives somewhere else. The human CTA is honest; the MACHINE claim overclaims. Pointing that url at the app would make it true in one line, but rewriting the structured data of 60 pages changes how the platform is presented in search - an outward-facing decision nobody can quietly reverse - so it is written up for Ian rather than done. Teeth-proven by restoring the exact old wording.

T156: a shared link should look intentional. T125 established what sharing here actually looks like - workers paste links into Viber and Messenger group chats - which makes the Open Graph card the first thing most people see of a page, often before the page itself. THE FINDING: 60 of ~116 public pages shipped NO og:image and no twitter:card, and they were all the /tools/ CALCULATORS - the top of the funnel, the pages most likely to be shared by a worker who just used one. Every one rendered as a bare grey link while the learn cluster's 53 articles rendered a proper card. public-feed had an image and a title but no og:description, so its card showed a headline, a picture, and whatever text the platform chose to guess. Fixed by reusing the SAME asset the learn cluster already uses rather than inventing a second one: two social images drift and one ends up stale. ★IT CHECKS THE IMAGE FILE EXISTS, not merely that the tag does - a card pointing at a missing PNG renders exactly like a card with no image, and the tag being present makes it look handled, which is the worst combination because nobody re-checks a field that is filled in. App pages are deliberately out of scope: a signed-in surface behind an auth wall is not shared to a group chat. Teeth-proven both ways - card removed RED, image pointed at a missing file RED.

T146: a hang must END, not spin forever. A fetch to an AI or transcription edge function is the one a plant floor will hang - a dead spot, a cold function, a slow uplink - and without a bound there is no failure at all, just a control stuck in its working state saying nothing. That is the eternal-skeleton shape wearing a spinner, and it is worse than an error because an error at least tells someone what to do next. THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: written after finding voice-journal's transcribeBlob unbounded, it immediately found THREE MORE - report-sender's transcribe, voice-handler's transcribe, and analytics' ORCHESTRATOR, the longest-running call on the platform, where a supervisor waiting on a report could not tell 'still thinking' from 'never coming back'. All four now route through the platform's own fetchWithTimeout rather than a second hand-rolled controller: it already owns the AbortController, the transport-retry policy and the null-on-abort contract. ★THE BOUNDS ARE SIZED FOR THE SLOWEST LEGITIMATE SUCCESS, NOT A DEVELOPER'S PATIENCE - 45s for a long spoken entry over a weak uplink, 120s for a full AI analytics phase - because a timeout tuned short turns working software into a lottery for the plants furthest from the server. Deliberately scoped to slow-by-nature endpoints: a quick REST read is already covered by whQueryTimeout, and demanding a timeout on every call in the codebase would be noise. ★CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (T40): this gate accepted a bare AbortController or a bare `signal:` as proof of a bound — and those are a CANCEL BUTTON, somewhere for a person to press, not a clock that fires on its own. analytics-report carried both and was still unbounded: the 22-page retry sweep graded it SILENT, sitting on 'Compiling analytics across all 4 phases' forever under a read outage because nothing would ever abort it if the reader simply waited — and this gate passed that page every run. A real bound now requires a TIMER: fetchWithTimeout, AbortSignal.timeout, a setTimeout that calls abort, or a Promise.race against a timed promise. The controller may still sit beside those (it is how the abort is delivered) but can no longer stand in for them. A --selftest pins all five cases, the first being the pre-fix analytics-report source, which must be RED.

T152: the teaching cluster is navigable in BOTH directions. 53 articles only teach as a cluster if a reader can move through them, and two different failures break that while being invisible to each other. AN ORPHAN is an article no hub link reaches: it exists, it is indexed, a searcher can land on it, and nobody browsing the library will ever find it - writing it was work that reaches nobody. A DEAD END is an article that links onward to nothing: a reader who finishes it has to go back and start again, which is where a session ends. Measured: 53 articles, 53 reachable from the hub, ZERO orphans, ZERO dead ends, and the hub links to nothing missing. The gate keeps it that way, because adding an article and forgetting the hub entry is a one-line omission nobody notices. ★IT ALSO CHECKS THE REVERSE OF AN ORPHAN - a hub link to an article that does not exist - because a library index offering a guide that 404s is worse than not listing it, and this cluster has been renamed before. ★AND ONWARD LINKS MUST REACH OTHER LEARN ARTICLES, not merely somewhere: a page whose only outbound link is a signup CTA is a dead end for a reader who came to learn, however many links it technically has. Teeth-proven by renaming one hub slug, which fired BOTH arms at once - the article became an orphan and the hub gained a promise it could not keep.

T151: a searcher's question answered above the fold, swept across all 53 learn articles. Somebody arrives from a search result with a question the snippet promised this page answers; what they meet in the first screen decides whether they stay, and the failure mode is not a broken page but one that opens with throat-clearing and buries the answer four scrolls down. ★THE ORACLE IS ANSWER-PRESENCE, NOT META-VERBATIM - T151 learned that the hard way when an earlier pass checked whether the meta description's words appeared on the page and produced a false red, because a description SUMMARIZES rather than quotes. Four assertions per article: an H1 exists; substantive opening prose follows it; that opening carries a distinctive term from the title; and a freshness stamp is visible, because a searcher landing on undated maintenance guidance cannot tell if it is current. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY VERDICT WAS TRUSTED, each found by READING the flags rather than acting on them: a {3,} filter silently dropped this platform's most important short terms (PM, AI, OEE) so an article opening 'Most Philippine plants run PMs' read as off-topic; an exact match called 'measurement' a miss for a title saying 'Measuring'; and scanning only

elements flagged the WorkHive-vs-MaintainX page, which opens with a textbook answer ('Choose MaintainX if... Choose WorkHive if...') written in a

of lines - the

tags it found were the byline and a repeated pricing disclaimer, so the gate read the furniture and missed the answer. It now reads VISIBLE TEXT, and allows one paragraph of runway, because enforcing sentence-one would legislate prose style rather than measure arrival. All 53 pass. Mutation-proven both ways: burying an answer behind preamble goes RED, and stripping a freshness stamp goes RED.

T138: a concurrency guard that says nothing is a LOST EDIT. An optimistic-concurrency guard filters an UPDATE on the row's updated_at so a write loses if somebody else changed the record first - that is the easy half. The half that decides whether it HELPS is what happens next: if nothing checks that ZERO ROWS changed, the update silently does nothing, the form closes, and the person walks away believing they saved work that no longer exists. A guard that returns without speaking is WORSE than no guard, because it converts a visible conflict into an invisible loss. ★THE CENSUS CORRECTED THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN RECORD: the basis read that logbook amends, community post edits and PM scope edits were 'presumed LAST-WRITE-WINS'. They are not. There are TEN hand-rolled guards across EIGHT pages (asset-hub, community, founder-console, integrations, logbook, platform-actions, pm-scheduler, project-manager x3) plus inventory through the central ocUpdate - eleven protected edit surfaces, not two - and every one of the ten detects the zero-row case AND tells the person. The gate does NOT demand migration to ocUpdate: that is ten rewrites of live edit paths for a refactor, and the property that protects a person is 'the guard SPEAKS', not 'the guard is shared'. The install-the-guard lesson still governs anything NEW - reach for ocUpdate first - and this exists so a hand-rolled one cannot ship silent. ★IT WOULD RATHER MISS THAN LIE: the window is the 40 lines after the filter, so a guard whose reporting lives further away reads as a miss, which is the safe direction for a gate whose other failure mode is a false accusation about working code. Teeth-proven with an injected silent guard.

oc-guard-speaks' own teeth (2026-10-13): its window is now the rest of the handler that holds the guard (brace-matched, at most 150 lines) instead of a fixed 40 - logbook's offline replay notices zero rows at +3 lines and says so at +63. Pinned three ways: a guard that speaks 60 lines later in the same handler passes, the same handler with no message fails, and a message in the NEXT function does not count.

T131: software that cannot count to one. '1 entries found', '1 assets', '1 parts' - individually trivial, collectively the thing that makes a product feel unfinished, and n=1 is not an edge case here: it is what a filtered list shows the moment a search gets specific. WHAT IS COUNTED is a count interpolated straight into a plural noun with NO singular branch nearby, and the count must be one that can GENUINELY be 1 - a .length, a *Count, a *_count, a *Total. Deliberately NOT cases like ${period} days, which is 30/60/90 by construction and never reads '1 days': the first pass of this measurement counted 82 that way, and a census padded with cases that cannot occur produces a number nobody trusts and a gate everyone learns to ignore. The honest figure was 30. ZERO IS NOT THE GOAL and this ratchet must not be read as demanding it - the sites span 13 files, mostly secondary and admin surfaces, and rewriting all of them in one sweep would be a large unreviewed change to render paths for a grammar nit. What was FIXED is the one a worker meets daily: the counter under the logbook's search box, which said '1 entries found' the moment a search narrowed to a single result. Baseline 27 after that fix; growth is the failure. The idiom to use is the platform's own, already present in several files - ${n} asset${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} - no helper and no new dependency. Teeth-proven by injecting one new offender: RED, then removed.

T166: 'who sees this?' answered where it is WRITTEN. Every write surface makes a person decide how candid to be, and that decision happens at the composer - answering it on a welcome card, a help page or a toast after the fact is answering it too late or to the wrong person. THE FINDING: voice-journal.html had ZERO audience statements while being the platform's MOST private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update AND delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row. The only place a worker was ever told lived on hive.html's join-flow welcome card: seen once, on a different page, at a moment they were not writing anything personal. A privacy guarantee a person cannot see is one they cannot rely on. THE WORDING IS READ OFF THE RLS, NEVER FROM MEMORY, and this trajectory carries the scar - a welcome card written the same week claimed the Voice Journal was the ONLY worker-private surface while the policies said otherwise (skill_profiles, badges and exam_attempts are auth_uid-scoped too). So the gate checks BOTH ENDS: the claim on the page AND the policies in the database, failing if a page claims a privacy the policies do not give - a promise the database does not keep being worse than no promise at all. Deliberately a SHORT NAMED LIST of surfaces where a person commits words others might read, not every input on the platform: a gate demanding an audience label on search boxes and filters would be switched off within a week. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix voice-journal.

T137: a promise to KEEP is as checkable as a promise to delete. The privacy policy states that compliance records (DOLE OSHS, ISO audit logs) are retained 10 years for general records and 15 for incident investigations - and this trajectory has ALREADY caught the platform making a retention promise it did not keep, claiming a 90-day retention of voice recordings when the product stores no audio at all. Measured 2026-08-26 and this promise holds: five retention crons exist and every one purges a TECHNICAL or DERIVED table (achievement_xp_log, agent_memory, embedding_cache, gateway_audit_log, hive_route_calls); none touches a compliance-class record, and hive_audit_log holds 9,019 rows with nothing scheduled to remove them. WHY IT NEEDS A GATE AND NOT A NOTE: that agreement is currently an accident of nobody having written the cron. Purging old logbook rows to save space is exactly what somebody adds on a slow afternoon, and the moment it lands a legal document about DOLE OSHS and ISO compliance becomes false - silently, with no user-visible symptom, because the records that would prove a plant's maintenance history in a regulatory dispute are precisely the ones nobody notices missing until they are needed. Asserts that no scheduled job deletes from logbook, pm_completions or hive_audit_log while the policy makes that promise; if the retention policy genuinely changes, the policy text and this list change together, which is the point of pairing them. It SKIPS rather than passes if the policy sentence disappears, so the gate cannot go quietly vacuous. Deliberately does NOT assert record AGES - nothing is 10 years old yet, so that check would pass forever without measuring anything. Teeth-proven by scheduling a logbook purge cron: RED, then removed.

T172: the terms may not promise what the product lacks. terms-of-service said, in two places, 'You may export your data at any time and delete your account' and 'You may stop using WorkHive and delete your account at any time'. NEITHER SURFACE EXISTS - there is no export-my-data control (T77) and no account-deletion door (T164). A marketing page overclaiming is bad; a TERMS page overclaiming is a promise at legal weight, made to a Philippine user exercising a PDPA right, and it is the document they would point to. THE FIX WAS NOT TO DELETE THE RIGHT: the right is real and the privacy policy already documents how it is honoured - email admin@workhiveph.com with the subject 'Data Rights Request'. The terms now say exactly that, and say plainly it is handled by hand rather than through a button. Same right, true sentence. Both the HTML and its .md twin were corrected, because a promise surviving in either copy is a promise still unkept. THE ASSERTION: no legal surface may claim a SELF-SERVE capability the product does not have - and each banned phrasing is PAIRED WITH THE CONTROL that would make it true, so the day somebody ships account deletion the claim becomes allowed by the same gate that forbids it now. NOT A PROSE LINT: it checks specific self-serve promises against specific missing controls, because a gate that graded legal writing would produce false reds forever and teach everyone to ignore it. Resurrection: RED on all three pre-fix claims.

T198: an 'it could not be computed' branch must be REACHABLE. A page that distinguishes 'computed, and the answer is nothing' from 'we could not compute it' has done the hard part of honest degradation - so the failure this catches is subtler and worse than not having the branch: the branch EXISTS, somebody wrote it deliberately, and the fallback hands it a value that can never trigger it. THE INSTANCE THAT PROVED THE CLASS: project-manager's renderCpm() guards `if (!cp)` and prints 'The critical path could not be computed right now', while its client fallback returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} } - AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY, so the guard never fired on the path it was written for, and a shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items' with a full Gantt beneath it. Fixed with critical_path: null. THE ASSERTION: where a consumer's if (!x) branch says something could not be computed, no producer in that file may assign x an empty-but-truthy value - measured at 11 such guards platform-wide and ZERO defeated, so the CLASS is extinct rather than the one instance being patched. ★AN EMPTY ARRAY AS A PLAIN DEFAULT IS NOT THIS: parts: [], rows: [], work: [] are correct ways to say 'none', and a first sweep flagged 33 of them; what makes it a defect is a consumer that DISTINGUISHES uncomputed from empty and a producer that collapses the distinction. ★AND THE DETECTOR FAILED ITS OWN RESURRECTION TEST FIRST - its producer pattern could not match a value containing nested braces, and the real defect contained slack_per_item: {}, so it reported 0 with the bug present. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than none; it now allows one nesting level and is proven to go 1 -> 0 across the fix.
No comment inside a tag (an HTML comment opened between an element's attributes is parsed as bogus attributes and silently drops what follows — the browser never errors)

Prod headers cover what ships (Content-Security-Policy must permit every external script/stylesheet the pages load and every requirement written into the source; Permissions-Policy must permit every browser API they call — an empty allowlist like geolocation=() denies our own pages too. _headers has no local equivalent, so all of it fails only in production, silently)

No eval under a strict CSP (the LIVE prod CSP in vercel.json has script-src without 'unsafe-eval', so any page-loaded same-origin script that uses eval()/new Function() throws on EVERY browser — the 2026-09-12 'browser too old' banner incident, where browser-floor.js's eval-based canary false-fired platform-wide the moment the CSP shipped. Reads the CSP Vercel actually serves, comment/string-strips before scanning, so a probe can never again require the one thing the policy forbids)

Celebration proportionality (the tier ladder and the round-number ladder live in different files and must not fire full-screen modals on consecutive level-ups — two celebrations in a row is one interruption, and it devalues the larger)

Status literals are classified (every status value the code WRITES must be one the consuming truth view classifies — a value permitted by a CHECK but bucketed by nothing is a value that means nothing)

T46/T105: ask for push when the worker WANTS it. A notification prompt at first paint is the fastest way to lose the permission permanently - the person has no reason to say yes yet, they say no, and the browser remembers that answer forever with no in-app way to undo it. There is no second chance, so WHEN the prompt fires matters more than how the feature is built. MEASURED - two call sites, both exemplary: marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush() runs from an onclick ('Turning on…') behind online/support/signed-in checks and refuses honestly when the answer is no ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications'); voice-handler's _requestPushPerm() fires ONLY when the worker has VERBALLY opted in (_isPushOptInReply) and only while the state is still 'default', inside the open user-gesture window, so a prior denial is never re-prompted. TWO ASSERTIONS: every requestPermission() sits behind a permission-state check or an explicit user action, and no call site is reachable from a load-time path. ★A LOOKBACK WINDOW CANNOT SEE A GESTURE BINDING, and the first version proved it by calling a correctly-gated prompt 'bare': svcEnablePush IS bound to an onclick 350 lines earlier, far outside any sane window. The binding is a property of the enclosing FUNCTION, not of nearby text, so the gate now resolves the function name and asks whether the file wires it to a click anywhere - the same structural-over-proximity correction that keeps coming up. ★IT CHECKS THE ASK, NOT THE FEATURE: whether push is wired, which VAPID key, whether the message is good all belong elsewhere; this is only about the one moment that cannot be taken back. Teeth proven with an injected DOMContentLoaded prompt.

T147: a failed write must not be silent. `if (!error) { paint }` with no else is the quietest bug this platform can ship - the write fails, the screen does not move, nothing is said, and from the user's side that is indistinguishable from a dead control. The natural next move is to press it again, which is how one silent refusal becomes repeated writes. FOUND ON community's toggleReaction, BOTH branches: tapping an emoji whose insert or delete failed left the count sitting still with no message. Fixed with the vocabulary the same page already owns (submitReply uses whWriteError), and the add path names the one case where doing nothing IS correct - a duplicate reaction (23505) says 'You have already reacted with this emoji' rather than reporting a failure the person cannot act on. VERIFIED LIVE with an injected 500: the count correctly does NOT move (no false optimistic paint) and the toast reads 'Your reaction was not saved. Tap again to retry.' MEASURED AFTER: 223 awaited db writes destructure `error` across the app pages and ZERO now guard with a bare `if (!error)` and no else; resurrection-proven, since removing the new else-branches puts the count back to 1. ★DELIBERATELY NARROW: it does not demand a particular message, nor that every write speak - plenty correctly stay quiet because the render that follows IS the receipt. It catches one specific shape, where the code explicitly took the error into its hands by destructuring it, branched on it, and then dropped it. That is never intentional.

T159: the page must say which language it is in. A screen reader picks its pronunciation rules from <html lang>, so Filipino text announced under lang='en' comes out as English phonemes applied to Tagalog - not accented, but unrecoverable. WCAG 3.1.1 asks for the page's language and 3.1.2 that a change of language be marked. ★THE HARD HALF IS THAT THIS PLATFORM IS BILINGUAL BY TOGGLE, NOT BY URL: one page, _t(en, fil) at every string, and a wh_lang preference - so the declaration is not a static fact set at build time, it has to FOLLOW the toggle, which is exactly the half a static audit misses. MEASURED and the discipline is clean: all 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent); utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own; and all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so switching mid-session updates the declaration without a reload. TWO ASSERTIONS: every public page carries <html lang>, and any page that writes the wh_lang preference must also assign documentElement.lang - a toggle that changes the words while leaving the declaration behind is WORSE than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in. ★NO hreflang IS ASSERTED, deliberately rather than by omission: hreflang describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language the reader chose, and demanding hreflang would be demanding a second site. Whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all is T159's open posture question and Ian's to answer; this gate holds the part that is true under either answer. Teeth proven on both halves.

T117 / WCAG 2.5.7: nothing may become reachable ONLY by dragging. A worker in gloves, a person with a tremor and anyone on a trackpad share one need - no function should require a dragging movement. The census found the platform CLEAN, and every gesture it has is harmless: nav-hub and companion-launcher let a person DRAG the floating button out of the way while opening it stays a TAP; session-timeout listens for touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, not a gesture requirement; wh-persona sets draggable=false, disabling dragging rather than requiring it. The one genuine keyboard trap in this family was already closed centrally - .wh-scroll-x regions scrolled by swipe were unreachable from a keyboard (axe scrollable-region-focusable, eight on project-report), fixed where the shared class lives rather than per call site. THE GATE FOUND A HIT ON ITS FIRST RUN and it was checked rather than assumed: integrations.html registers a drop handler for CMMS imports - and it is guarded by if (dropZone && fileInput), with a real labelled input type=file wired to the SAME handleFile on change. Drag-and-drop over a working file picker is exactly what 2.5.7 asks for, so it is justified by name with that reason recorded. A NEW gesture file fails - not because dragging is forbidden, but because 'is there a tap that does the same thing?' is a question somebody must answer out loud before it ships. Scoped to product surfaces: vendor bundles and the measurement tooling whose JOB is to find drag handlers are excluded, since a lens that greps for dragstart would otherwise fail a gate about dragstart. ★MERGED WITH T75 (2026-08-26), which asked the same question of dayplanner and found it has NO drag machinery at all - the walk's premise was wrong, there was no drag to alternate. That pass added the rule that now decides the FAB repositioners: a handler assigning only style.left/right/top/bottom MOVES a control and confers no capability, so it passes, while one that also mutates data (insert, splice, sort_order) is load-bearing and must offer a tap. Deciding by what the handler WRITES rather than by which file it lives in keeps the exemption from becoming a licence. ★AND A REAL MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: driving T75 I wrote a second version of this gate straight over the T117 file, having read 'updated successfully' as 'created', then removed 102 unrelated gate registrations with an over-greedy cleanup regex. The duplicate-id guard caught the first, a HEAD diff caught and repaired the second. A duplicate id is a signal to MERGE two efforts, never to register the same name twice.

T106's arrival-fidelity oracle for EMAIL. Every 'View in WorkHive' link in send-report-email pointed at a bare page root, so a PM Overdue report - a document whose entire subject IS the overdue set - landed its reader on the unfiltered schedule, and both logbook reports landed on that page's default MINE view while the report itself is hive-wide: T19's two-windows-one-metric mismatch arriving by email, at whoever the supervisor forwarded it to. Measured before changing anything - ?filter=overdue is a real chip value on pm-scheduler AND genuinely filters (live: ontrack 0 rows, duesoon 2, overdue 10 vs 10 bare), so the parameter works rather than merely highlighting a chip. THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS is not that links carry params but that every param they carry is one the TARGET PAGE ACTUALLY READS, checked against the generated param_route_registry: a link decorated with ?window=7d would look more specific while delivering nothing, which is worse than a bare link because it reads as context that was never handed over. Also asserts every target page exists - a link into a renamed page is a dead end reached from an inbox, where nobody can press Retry. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: that all eight carry a param; five target analytics.html and project-manager.html, which read NO params at all, so their links are already as specific as those pages allow and demanding more would push someone to invent one that does nothing. Resurrection BOTH ways: RED on the pre-fix bare links, and RED again on a mutation adding a plausible ?window=90d that analytics never reads.

T107's one-honest-concept oracle for 'things for me'. The hive board's bell held four entries on the live board - PM Due Soon, Assets With PM Overdue, Open work orders, Low stock - every one a PLANT CONDITION already painted as a tile on the same page and again in alert-hub, blended with the approval entries, which are the only ones actually about the person reading them: one bell, two concepts, no way to tell which you were looking at. And the only unread signal was a 3% white tint on a dark surface, present in code and invisible in use, so a badge over ten rows gave no way to see WHICH were new. Asserts STRUCTURE, never wording: the two lanes are named, the plant lane links to the surface that owns those conditions, unread carries a marker BOTH a sighted user and a screen reader can find, and every pushNotif type is classified - a new one lands here as a decision rather than drifting into whichever lane the default sends it. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix page for 3 of 4, and the 4th mutation-proven with an injected 'mention' producer.

T63: a page may not ANNOUNCE a write it never confirmed (2026-08-27). The mirror of unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure, and the worse half — telling someone their work failed when it landed costs a retry; telling them it SAVED when it did not is a lie they act on: they close the tab, walk away from the machine, stop chasing the payment. ★supabase-js DOES NOT THROW WHEN A WRITE IS REFUSED — it resolves with { error } — so `try { await db.from(t).delete()… } catch` is not protection: the catch only ever sees THROWN errors and an RLS refusal never throws. Same root as the bare-builder class seen from the other end (there the promise was never sent; here it was sent, refused, and the refusal discarded). ★IT FOUND ONE, IN THE WORST PLACE: integrations' rollbackBatch ran three writes — delete from external_sync, delete the imported rows from the target table, mark the audit entry rolled back — discarded all three results and said 'Import rolled back successfully.' A refusal on any step left every imported row in place while the person was told the import had been undone. On a REVERSAL that is the worst available lie: they stop looking and the bad data stays in the hive. Fixed, so this gate carries NO baseline — any hit is new. ★A ROWS-RETURNED CHECK COUNTS: pm-scheduler verifies with `if (upgraded && upgraded.length)` instead of reading `error`, which is equally valid; an earlier draft of the detector called that a defect, so the rule accepts either shape. Teeth (--selftest, 5 cases) incl. both valid check shapes and an error-toast that is not a success claim. Static, read-only.

T176: an empty RETURNING is an UNCONFIRMED write, not a failed one (2026-08-27). supabase-js resolves `.insert(...).select(...)` with { data: [], error: null } when the INSERT SUCCEEDED and the RETURNING read was refused — RLS gates SELECT separately from INSERT. So `if (!data || !data.length)` has learned exactly one thing: the write is unconfirmed. It has NOT learned that it failed. Eighteen sites branch this way; eight told the user their work was lost, and two were actively dangerous because the advice was 'try again': re-hailing broadcasts a SECOND job to every nearby provider for work the client wants done once, and re-registering creates a second provider profile for the same hive. ★EACH OF THOSE WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE — the hail has a catalog path and a custom-scope path, registration has a hive path and a freelancer path — and the sweep's dedup-by-message had hidden the twins; the editor refusing an ambiguous match is what exposed them. All four now say what is actually known ('may have been sent — we could not confirm it') and point at the LIST rather than back at the button. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY SPOKE CORRECTLY in four other places ('the job may have moved on', 'that top-up was already decided', 'changed since you opened it, reloading'), which makes the eight a drift rather than a gap. ★THE BASELINE IS FULLY TRIAGED AGAINST THE SCHEMA, never waved through: every survivor is an idempotent UPDATE, an UPSERT with onConflict, or an INSERT the database makes un-duplicatable (service_vouchers_code_key UNIQUE on code; marketplace_reviews_one_per_request_direction UNIQUE). Where a retry cannot cost anything, 'try again' is honest advice even if 'didn't save' is imprecise — a wording item, not a hazard. A baseline holding UNTRIAGED entries would launder unknowns as accepted, the failure na-premise-holds exists to prevent. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases). Static, read-only.

T176: whReadError's second argument is SPLICED MID-SENTENCE (2026-08-27). The helper does not print `what` — it composes 'Your session expired, so ' + thing + ' could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it.' — so it must receive a NOUN PHRASE ('your equipment list', 'the audit log'). Four callsites passed a whole SENTENCE, and what shipped was: "Your session expired, so Could not load your equipment list. Check your connection. could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it. Nothing you did was lost." MEASURED in the browser, not reasoned — the same call with a noun returns the sentence it should. ★THE MISTAKE HAD A GOOD MOTIVE, which is why it needs a gate and not a scolding: each site was CONVERTED from a hand-rolled message to the taxonomy helper — exactly the right move — and the old sentence was forwarded into the argument slot. logbook even carries a comment above it explaining that the upstream sentence belongs in console.error and never in the notice; the author understood the principle and still handed the helper a sentence. Converting to the taxonomy means REPLACING the sentence with a noun, not passing it through. ★AND IT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER CHECK: the helper is present, so an adoption sweep passes it; the string holds no raw error text, so the raw-echo ratchet passes it; nothing throws. Only reading the composed sentence shows it — and that sentence only appears when a session dies mid-read, which is precisely when nobody is watching. whWriteError and whAiError are OUT OF SCOPE by design: their second argument IS a fallback message. Teeth (--selftest, 7 cases) incl. both out-of-scope helpers and a verb-opener with no period. Static, read-only.

T105: a table the UI writes should have a READER (2026-08-27). The table-level twin of captured-columns-reach-a-reader — that one asks which COLUMNS never reach a person, this asks which whole TABLES the UI fills and never opens again. ★IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN: marketplace-seller writes push_subscriptions when a provider enables job alerts and never reads one back, and the push card renders only while `Notification.permission !== 'granted'` — so the moment permission is granted the card vanishes forever and NOTHING ever confirms a subscription row exists. Browser permission and a live subscription are different facts: the endpoint rotates, the service worker is replaced, an upsert fails, a row is cleared, and permission stays 'granted' through every one of them — leaving the provider shown nothing while believing the page's own promise that they will 'hear new hails with this tab closed'. Measured at 0 rows. The table having no reader is precisely what let the page never check; the fix gave the card a third state ('granted but not actually subscribed', with a one-tap repair) and thereby gave the table its reader. ★READS THROUGH VIEWS COUNT, and that is the whole difficulty: naively 14 of 54 written tables looked write-only, including community_posts, hives and service_requests — all read constantly, through TRUTH VIEWS (community reads v_community_posts_truth). Resolving view→base-table from information_schema took 14 down to 2, and both survivors were real. A sweep that cannot see through a view manufactures a dozen false findings. ★A FAILED READ MUST NOT ACCUSE: the page's lookup returns null for UNKNOWN and only an explicit false warns, so a refused read can never tell a correctly-subscribed provider their alerts are off. Ratchet: the one survivor (early_access_emails — service_role-only RLS, an Ian decision on T67) is baselined with its reason. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. the view-resolution case in both directions. Needs the local DB for the view map; SKIPs rather than guesses when it is down.

T15: a column written for a PERSON must reach one (2026-08-27). logbook captured loto_applied, permit_reference, readings_json and failure_consequence on its form, stored them on the row, restored them into the EDIT FORM when an entry was edited, and rendered them to a reader NOWHERE — 1,767 of 3,811 entries carried equipment readings nobody could see. ★THE PHANTOM-COLUMN AUDITOR CANNOT CATCH THIS: it asks whether a column has a READ CONSUMER, and a `.select('loto_applied')` satisfies it. SELECTED IS NOT RENDERED — that gap is the whole finding. Asked platform-wide over 121 written columns it returned 9, and project_roles.assigned_by was a real one: 36 of 36 rows record who assigned a project role and the pill showed the name alone, so 'who put me on this?' had no answer in the app (fixed; the sweep now confirms it dropped off the list). A RATCHET, not a cliff — the survivors are baselined WITH their verdicts, because the triage is the valuable part. THREE are FIXED and deliberately absent from the baseline so a regression fails this gate: assigned_by, variance_reason (the provider's finished-job card now reports the amount, method, reference and the payer's reason) and provider_type (the quote card now says 'Hive team' or 'Freelancer' where a buyer chooses). Of the rest: 3 are NOT defects (timestamps whose fact the rendered status already carries; a total the page shows as its two parts), 2 are unused rather than withheld (MEASURED at 0 rows — live_location has never been populated, so no client is being denied it), and 1 is a raw auth uid whose display would trade this defect for the no-raw-internals one. ★SCOPE IS PLATFORM-WIDE ON PURPOSE: per-page it reported ~30 false candidates, because pages WRITE audit rows (actor/target_id/target_name/target_type) and the AUDIT-LOG page renders them. ★AND WRITERS ≠ RENDERERS: shared scripts count as renderers so a column shown by utils.js is not 'invisible', but treating them as writers too pulled in ten AI-telemetry columns (response_time_ms, model_confidence…) written for a machine, not a person. Credential columns (key_hash, p256dh, auth uids) are excluded outright — not rendering those is the security property. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. cross-page rendering, form-restore-is-not-rendering, and secrets. Static, read-only.

A read that FAILED must not render as 'there is nothing' (2026-08-27). The shape: a loader catches, blanks its list, toasts, re-renders. The toast FADES; the empty state is what stays — so an unread table ends as 'No pending listings' or 'be the first to sell', factual CLAIMS about the world made at the exact moment the platform could not read it. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNEW, TWICE: marketplace.html carries the diagnosis in its own source from a deepwalk ('the toast alone was insufficient — it fades, leaving the GRID showing the first-run CTA on a full marketplace') and sets _loadError; marketplace-seller-profile carries its own ('Only a read that ANSWERED may license a conclusion about this seller') and sets _reviewsFailed. Both fixed. marketplace-admin — the MODERATION queue, where 'nothing to review' is the sentence most likely to make someone stop looking — never got the fix, and neither did dayplanner's plant-PM rail, which on a failed read returned '' and simply VANISHED (a worker cannot tell an absent section from a quiet day). Second fix-that-did-not-travel this session; a lesson in one file's source protects that file, a gate makes it the platform's. ★THE RULE: a catch that blanks a list on a page owning an empty state must record that the read failed. The flag's NAME is not prescribed — three pages spell it three ways (_loadError, _reviewsFailed, _readFailed.listings) and all three are correct. ★SCOPED TO LOADERS: the catch must wrap a query, because not every `catch { x = [] }` is a load failure — alert-hub falls back to [] when a legacy double-encoded parts field will not parse, which is correct, and the first version of this gate called it a defect. Teeth: 5 selftest cases incl. bare and property-style flags.

T29: acting on an alert must make the ALERT GO AWAY (2026-08-27). An alert inbox that never empties is an inbox people stop reading, so the chain has to close: the alert names an action, links to where that action is taken, and DOING it removes the alert — with nobody marking anything by hand. ★THE CLOSURE IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST KIND: alert-hub's PM alerts are DERIVED, not stored — they come from v_pm_scope_items_truth filtered is_overdue=true, so there is no status to update and no second write to forget. Complete the PM and the row simply stops matching. PROVEN LIVE rather than reasoned: inserting a 'done' completion for an overdue scope item inside a transaction takes its overdue count 1 → 0 and moves days_until_due −34 → +7, then rolls back with zero residue. ★TWO ASSERTIONS, because either alone is a half-truth — THE LINK EXISTS (an href to pm-scheduler for the NAMED asset plus an action label; an alert that states a problem and offers no way to it is a notification, not an inbox item) and THE CONDITION CLEARS (a link to a surface that does not actually resolve the alert leaves the loop open while looking closed). ★The gate's own link check was wrong first: a lazy any-character match ending at the first closing brace stopped INSIDE the first nested brace — inside a template expression, well before href and actionLabel — and reported a correctly-linked alert as offering no way to act. Read as a plain forward window now, because that is what the block is.

T11: a deduction that moved NOTHING must not read as success (2026-08-27). Two workers finish repairs on the same part; inventory_deduct locks the item FOR UPDATE so the race is serialised, and the loser's call runs against an empty shelf. ★WHAT THE LOSER GOT, MEASURED LIVE (real item set to 0 inside a rolled-back transaction): `v_qty := GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)` CLAMPS instead of refusing, so asking for 1 with 0 on the shelf returned 0, wrote a ledger row with qty_change 0, changed nothing, and raised NO error. Every caller checked only `error`, so the worker was told 'Entry saved' while their entry claimed a part the shelf never gave up — the shelf and the system disagreeing silently, which is the one thing this trajectory exists to prevent. ★AND THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT TELL THEM APART: it is the new quantity, and 'took the last one' and 'there were none' both end at 0. The LEDGER row can, because it records what MOVED — so callers pass p_txn_id (the function always accepted one) and read that row back through whDeductMoved(); verified under RLS that a member can read their own hive's inventory_transactions row. ★THREE SITES, NOT ONE: logbook's SAVE path, logbook's EDIT path, and inventory's Use modal — and inventory additionally cached `addTransaction(..., -qty, ...)`, recording the amount ASKED, so the page's own transaction list claimed a movement the database never made; it now records what moved. The first version of this GATE had the same disease it was built to catch, grading only the first call it found with re.search while two others kept the defect. ★TEETH (--selftest): the pre-fix error-only shape goes RED, an id passed but never read back goes RED, id+readback+comparison passes, and every live site is asserted green. The DB half rolls back and re-reads the shelf to prove it.

T19: hiding a plant alert is a HIVE action and must say so (2026-08-27). alert_dismissals is keyed onConflict 'hive_id,alert_key' — ONE row per alert per hive — so every control that writes it changes what the WHOLE CREW sees: marking handled, snoozing, and marking seen alike. Nothing about the surface said that. The local state is `_seen`, the control is an aria-pressed toggle, the copy was two words: everything reads personal bookmark while the write is shared state. ★THE FAILURE IS WRITTEN IN dismissAlert's OWN COMMENT — 'a plant alert quietly blinded for the whole crew by someone who thought they were tidying their own view' — and that path was fixed when it was written while its SIBLING acknowledgeAlert was not: nothing about scope on the way in, and on the way out (un-marking DELETES the hive's row and returns the alert to unseen for everyone) nothing at all, so the crew could watch an alert reappear with no idea who or why. Both now name the scope and the actor, in EN and FIL. ★THE RULE: every user-facing message on a successful alert_dismissals write must name the scope, matched by MEANING across both languages rather than a fixed sentence — the copy ships bilingual via _t(en, fil), and a gate that pins wording punishes improving it. ★TEETH ARE THE PRE-FIX WORLD VERBATIM (--selftest, 5 cases): the old `_t('Marked seen', 'Minarkahang nakita')` is the 'two words with no scope' RED, and the old un-mark is the 'silent write' RED; a read-only query owes nothing and stays green. ★The gate's own window was wrong first and its selftest caught it: a fixed 900-char scan ended before both announcements (they sit past a writeAuditLog call and a long comment) and reported two correct paths as silent, so the search is now bounded by the `catch (` that actually ends the success path.

T7: the code still works, and the door is still shut (2026-08-27). A removed worker usually still HAS the invite code — read aloud at a briefing, sitting in a chat thread — so rejoining is not an edge case, it is the next thing that happens, and it has two halves that must agree. ★THE DOOR, asserted LIVE: join_hive_by_code refuses a kicked member twice over — by auth identity, and again by (hive, worker_name) so a second account cannot walk a ban back in. Both are driven, because 'the function has an IF' is not 'the function refuses', and the second branch only fires for an identity with no membership row at all, which is exactly the shape a reading of the source talks itself out of. ★AND THE SENTENCE: a refusal reaching a person as a raw code, or as 'could not join', says the app is broken rather than that a decision was made about them. hive.html must key on HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED and say WHAT (removed) and WHAT NOW (a way that is not retrying the code, since retrying is the one action that cannot work) — matched by MEANING, not a fixed sentence, because a fixed sentence is a gate that fails when someone improves the wording. Distinct from removal-tells-the-worker (T25), which covers the removed worker's ARRIVAL; this covers the door they knock on afterwards. ★SAFETY: the kicked state is created inside a transaction and ROLLED BACK, verified by re-reading the member's status. ★TEETH (--teeth): Postgres has transactional DDL, so the run replaces join_hive_by_code with a permissive version INSIDE the same transaction — both branches then report 'allowed' and the gate fails naming both, while the definition is re-read afterwards to prove the real function came back. A green teeth run would mean this gate cannot see an open door. ★The copy check itself was caught wrong by its own selftest first: a naive quote-to-quote regex paired the closing quote of one literal with the opening quote of the next and read the CODE between them, so a correct page looked silent.
Auto-discovery Validator (HTML classified, edge fns in config, validators registered)

Storage-Key Registry (PLATFORM_CENTRALIZATION C-P4: every localStorage/sessionStorage key is CANONICAL or a registered ALIAS in storage_key_registry.json; a new UNKNOWN key FAILs until registered — stops the wh_active_hive_id/wh_hive_id drift class)

HIVE-CAPTURE INVARIANT — a load-time hive capture is only safe while nothing can change the active hive mid-page. marketplace.html does `const HIVE_ID = whHiveId()` once at load and stamps it on every hail and listing, so if the active hive could change while the page is open, work would be filed into the WRONG TENANT. It cannot today: the only pages that write `wh_active_hive_id` are hive.html (the switcher) and index.html (the sign-in bootstrap), and reaching the marketplace from either is a full page load, so the const is always read fresh. That was recorded as the A4 finding on `TB-A345-architecture-quality` — no defect — and it is a conclusion resting on an invariant nobody enforced: add an in-page hive switcher to the marketplace and every subsequent hail carries a stale tenant id with no test going red. Per this platform's disposition rule, a covered-by-nature cell still gets a gate asserting the contract it rests on. TWO ASSERTIONS: (A) the WRITER ALLOWLIST — exactly hive.html and index.html may write the key, and a third page appearing goes red with the instruction to re-check capture scope on every page that reads it, because adding a writer is a decision rather than automatically a bug; (B) THE CAPTURING PAGES MUST NOT WRITE IT — marketplace.html / marketplace-seller.html / marketplace-admin.html must contain zero writers, which is the live-bug condition, since a writer in the same document can run after the capture. CHECKING THE PREMISE CORRECTED THE FINDING TWICE, both errors mine: the cell claimed every write lives on hive.html (index.html:2953 writes it too — the conclusion survived, the stated premise was false), and index.html ALSO reads whHiveId() into a `const HIVE_ID`, which looks like the same stale-capture shape but is not, because that capture is FUNCTION-scoped inside the ops-home renderer (re-read per call) and the write is deliberately followed by `_initDashboard(...)` to re-render against the new hive — verified by reading both sites rather than trusting the comment. So the distinction that matters is SCOPE, not filename. The gate deliberately does NOT try to compute JS scope from a regex: brace and regex-literal counting over inline script is the brittle-validator trap this platform has already been bitten by, so it asserts the two cheap, unarguable properties instead. Self-test injects a writer into marketplace.html THROUGH THE READER (no file on disk is touched, the same discipline as injecting a mutant inside a transaction) and requires the gate to go red naming that page — without it, a green result would mean nothing. Static file scan, fast, always runs.

PUSH HANDLER CONTRACT — a delivered push must actually reach the person. FOUND 2026-07-30 while dispositioning the test bank's TB-S5-edge-push-delivery-roundtrip cell, whose note read 'nothing proves a real subscription RENDERS the notification'. Checked rather than assumed: the SEND side is well covered (notify-push is VAPID-signed and was proven E2E against the real FCM service) and TWO service-worker validators already exist — validate_sw_offline and validate_sw_shell_membership — but NEITHER mentions push, showNotification or notificationclick even once. The receive side had no gate at all. That gap matters because every failure mode is SILENT, and sw.js says so itself: 'Without these handlers a delivered push silently no-ops.' The push arrives, the worker wakes, nothing appears, and nothing errors anywhere a person or a log would see it — a provider just misses the job. SEVEN invariants, each a silent failure: (1) a `push` listener exists (else the push is delivered and discarded); (2) the handler calls showNotification (else the worker wakes and renders nothing); (3) that call is INSIDE event.waitUntil — brace-matched, and the check requires waitUntil to WRAP it rather than merely appear in the handler, because a bare showNotification works on a warm worker and fails on a cold one, which is the hardest kind of bug to reproduce; (4) e.data.json() is guarded by try/catch, since a non-JSON payload THROWS and one malformed push then silently suppresses the notification; (5) a `notificationclick` listener exists (else the tap does nothing); (6) it focuses a tab or opens one (else the notification is a dead end); (7) it closes the notification (else the tray keeps an item the user already acted on). Static by design — these are properties of the file that ships to installed PWAs, and the CACHE_NAME comment records the cost of getting it wrong: 'without this bump installed PWAs keep the handler-less worker'. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: the OS notification tray is outside any harness, so 'the human saw it' stays unprobeable; the runtime tier (dispatch a push event to a registered worker and assert showNotification fired) remains recorded as owed with this gate named as its first half, so the residual gap has a shape instead of a shrug. Self-test proves all 7 hold on the shipped worker AND that five deliberately broken workers are each caught.

T82: edge refusals reach the user — the static census. supabase-js collapses EVERY non-2xx from functions.invoke into ONE FunctionsHttpError whose message is the literal string "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code". The status and body survive only on error.context (a Response), so a caller reading error.message never sees them - and shows that placeholder to a person. ★THE CLIENT THEN SILENTLY UNDOES THE WORK THE BACKEND DID: rate-limit.ts answers a drained hive with 429 and "AI call limit reached for this hive. Try again in an hour." - cause named, clearing time named, exactly the bar the AI-error taxonomy exists to hold. MEASURED on asset-hub (met by genuinely exhausting the hourly quota): the worker read "Could not reach Asset Brain: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code", a CONNECTION-flavoured sentence for a QUOTA event, sending them to check their signal instead of waiting an hour. whAiError could not rescue it either - it keys on /429|rate.?limit|quota/ and the placeholder carries none of them. Fixed centrally: utils.js whFnError() reads error.context, so the function's own sentence survives and only a body-less failure falls back to the status taxonomy. The unwrap had been hand-rolled in companion-launcher, analytics and assistant - three copies, thirteen other files without it. WHAT IT COUNTS: invoke error branches that put error.message in front of a person (toast, innerHTML, textContent, a whListError/whReadError call) without consulting error.context or whFnError. ★IT COUNTS RATHER THAN FORBIDS - 39 invoke sites, 19 speaking the placeholder at first measure; a gate that failed all of them on day one would be turned off. Forward-only against tools/edge_refusal_baseline.json; asset-hub's four sites were cleared in the same pass, 19 -> 16. ★AND IT ONLY FLAGS BRANCHES THAT SPEAK: an invoke whose error is logged, swallowed or rethrown shows nobody the placeholder, and charging for it would measure code shape rather than harm.

T84: new claims are opt-in — T84's resume-polish oracle (2026-08-26). resume.html's review sheet is a good pattern: the AI only SUGGESTS, and nothing reaches the document until the worker approves it. But two different acts arrived with the same default. REWRITE - polishing a bullet the worker wrote - is shown as 'Was: <their text>' and pre-ticked; their content, improved, with the change visible, which is fine. ADD - the 'suggested highlights' from tailor_to_jd - is PUSHED into their experience, was also pre-ticked, and carries no 'Was:' because there is no before. Those are NET-NEW CLAIMS ABOUT THE WORKER, generated with the JOB AD in context: exactly the pressure that produces a line they cannot back up in an interview, on the document they hand an employer. FOUND: both checked:true, so the default path (Tailor, then Apply) added up to five such claims without one deliberate act of accepting any. The prompt DOES instruct the model to keep highlights truthful and grounded in stated skills - worth having, and kept - but a prompt is the only thing enforcing it, and pre-ticking removed the human check meant to be the backstop. New claims now start unchecked, and the tailored summary gained its 'Was:' so its diff is visible like the polish path's. ★IT READS THE APPLY FUNCTION, NOT THE LABEL: addition versus edit is decided by what it does to the document (.push vs assignment), which no wording can disguise. ★AND IT DOES NOT BAN PRE-TICKING - making every suggestion opt-in would push workers toward tapping Apply without reading, the very behaviour this prevents; only new claims about a person carry the burden. ★ITS OWN MATCHER WAS BLIND FIRST: it bounded the apply body with [^;]{0,400} and every real apply is several statements long, so it matched nothing and PASSED against the world it was built to catch - caught only by teeth-proving, which is why it is not registered vacuous.

T89: converted money states its rate — the owner's AI-cost oracle (2026-08-26). ai-quality's cost card is the owner's answer to 'what is this costing me'. Every peso figure on it - the hero, the per-call average, and the MODEST / TYPICAL / HEAVY verdict thresholds - came from one hardcoded constant, PHP_PER_USD = 56, which was neither dated nor shown. PHP/USD has moved between roughly 50 and 59 in recent years, so a drifting rate silently shifts both the number and the JUDGEMENT about it, while the card reads like a measurement. The figure is not so much wrong as unfalsifiable: an owner cannot tell whether ₱2,100 means 'heavy use' or 'the rate is stale'. The rate is now stated beside the figure, the way a source chip states a window. ★IT DOES NOT DEMAND A LIVE RATE - a fixed rate is a reasonable choice for a cost estimate; presenting the result as if nothing was assumed is not. Checked and found CORRECT rather than manufactured into a defect: the conversion itself is sound (php = totalCost * PHP_PER_USD, and the thresholds compare pesos to pesos), and the details table's USD figure is labelled as USD. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the rate is undisclosed and the gate names the line.

T89: the quota warns before the wall — a count is not a warning (2026-08-26). _shared/rate-limit.ts returns `remaining` on EVERY allowed call, so the platform always knows how close a hive is to its hourly cap. An absent reading is not a reading of zero; it is now silent. ★IT DOES NOT REQUIRE EVERY AI SURFACE TO SHOW A QUOTA - most never receive `remaining`, and demanding that plumbing everywhere would make this a migration rather than a gate; it holds the surfaces that DO show it to showing it usefully. ★AND ITS OWN MATCHER WAS BLIND FIRST: it looked for 'whQuotaNotice(' while utils.js defines it as 'whQuotaNotice = function', so it reported the helper missing while it sat ten lines above - it would have failed forever on a correct file. Teeth: pre-fix it flags both the bare render and the absent helper.

T185: two people who share a name both get into the hive (2026-08-26).
